description:
A large four-legged swamp reptile with a naturally long, low body, long tail, strong jaws, copper-orange scales and teal dorsal spines. It has no carried items or recorded wealth. The replacement art keeps the saved two-square-wide by one-square-high footprint and shows a reaching near foreclaw plus open-mouthed forward bite in action.

IMAGEGEN PROMPT - READY:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: ready frame for OpenGold combat sprite MON8CHA.DAX:59/default; later exported as 128x128 transparent PNG.
Primary request: Create ONE new original giant swamp lizard in a low, long stalking ready pose facing SCREEN RIGHT. This is a powerful four-legged reptile, not a dragon: elongated natural lizard torso and tail, four anatomically connected scaled legs, broad toothy lizard jaws, alert yellow eyes, copper-orange scales, restrained teal highlights and short teal dorsal spines, pale tan throat and belly. No wings, horns, armor, weapons, jewelry or carried objects. Keep the species identity close to the current copper-and-teal giant lizard while redesigning its proportions naturally for a wide, low silhouette.
Animation plan: Both hind paws and the far front paw are planted, with their locations defining the stationary base for the action frame. The near front claw is held slightly raised and bent close to the chest, ready to reach to screen right. The head points right with its mouth mostly closed. Reserve transparent space ahead of the head and near foreclaw for the later bite and reaching-claw action.
Composition: Full body in side-to-front-three-quarter view, long tail extended LOW toward screen left, head toward screen right. Fit a TWO COMBAT SQUARES WIDE BY ONE SQUARE HIGH silhouette without squashing the anatomy: the visible creature should be approximately twice as wide as it is tall, including tail and low dorsal spines. Do not curl the tail or lift spines so high that the silhouette becomes square. All parts remain inside a single transparent canvas with margins. The fixed combat grid is not drawn.
Style: crisp readable classic fantasy game pixel art with strong lizard silhouette, detailed scales that remain legible at small combat size, true transparency.
Constraints: One frame only, not an animation sheet. Exactly four legs and four claws. No extra limbs, painted background, ground shadow, smoke, magic, text, border, or clipped tail. Create independent art; do not copy original game artwork.

IMAGEGEN PROMPT - ACTION:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: action frame for OpenGold combat sprite MON8CHA.DAX:59/default; later exported as 128x128 transparent PNG.
Input image: the newly generated ready giant lizard is the EDIT TARGET and exact identity/registration reference. Do not use original game artwork.
Primary request: Make a clear joint claw-and-bite ATTACK toward SCREEN RIGHT. The near front claw, already poised in ready, reaches farther and more forcefully to the right with spread talons, visibly leading the strike. The head and neck lunge forward toward screen right; open the upper and lower jaws WIDE with teeth and dark mouth interior visible, as if snapping at a target. The upper chest may lean modestly into the bite, but remain continuously attached to the belly and rear torso.
Animation registration: Keep the exact same copper-orange and teal giant lizard, scale, camera and canvas origin. Both hind paws and the far front paw remain planted at the exact same x/y locations as in ready. The tail base, hips and rear belly stay registered. Move only the attacking near forelimb plus head, neck and modest upper chest; do not shift, shrink, stretch, independently crop or rotate the whole animal. Preserve precisely four connected legs, one long low tail, short dorsal spines and the same head identity.
Footprint: The body fits TWO combat squares wide and ONE square high in both frames. The reaching claw and bite remain inside the transparent PNG with margin. Use the same export transform for ready and action; do not change one frame's scale to fit.
Style: Same crisp fantasy game pixel art and true transparency as the edit target. One figure, one frame.
Avoid: closed-mouth roar, claw aimed toward the viewer instead of screen right, extra legs, floating claw, detached chest, new gear, wings, magic effects, scenery, ground shadow, text, border, opaque background or sprite sheet.
